reading: The input is all background; the output paints the grid's outer border with colour 8 and leaves the inside empty.

new_rows.name: rim
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rim(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
rim(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0.
rim(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), maxy(M), Y = M.
rim(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), maxx(M), X = M.

why: every border cell becomes 8; interior cells stay 0; same size

reading: Row 1 starts with a short seed of colours; the seed colours are repeated cyclically along the row at triangular-number positions 0,1,3,6,10,15,21,28,... (gaps growing by one).

slots.seed: the non-background colours at the start of the middle row, in order
slots.positions: triangular numbers n(n+1)/2 that fit in the row
slots.colour: seed[n mod len(seed)] at position n(n+1)/2

why: output middle row has colour seed[n mod k] exactly at columns n(n+1)/2 and 0 elsewhere; other rows unchanged

reading: A horizontal line of 1s contains some 8 and 2 cells; from each 8 a stalk grows upward of two 1s capped by an 8, and from each 2 a stalk of three 1s capped by a 2.

slots.anchors: cells of the line that are not colour 1 (8 or 2)
slots.body: colour 1 cells: 2 for an 8 anchor, 3 for a 2 anchor
slots.tip: one cell of the anchor's colour above the body

why: above each 8 in the line: 1,1,8; above each 2: 1,1,1,2; everything else unchanged

reading: Every 4 cell falls down one row; a 4 that lands directly on top of the 2 line splashes, drawing diagonal 4-lines up-left and up-right to the grid border.

slots.subject: isolated 4 cells (markers)
slots.trigger: new position is immediately above a 2 cell
slots.lines: two diagonals from the landed cell going up-left and up-right until the border, colour 4

why: each 4 appears one row lower; landed-on-line 4s emit both upward diagonals; 2 line unchanged

reading: Two bars of one colour sit on the top and bottom rows with a 2 separator line between; the columns both bars share are filled with 4 between the longer bar and the separator.

new_rows.name: gap
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
bar(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
bar(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), maxy(M), Y = M.
bsize(O, count(Y, X)) :- bar(O), obj(O, Y, X).
big(O) :- bsize(O, N), bsize(P, K), N > K.
small(O) :- bsize(O, N), bsize(P, K), N < K.
bigcol(X) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).
smallcol(X) :- small(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bigrow(B) :- big(O), obj(O, B, X).
seprow(S) :- cell(S, X, C), maxy(M), S > 0, S < M.
gap(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), bigcol(X), smallcol(X), bigrow(B), seprow(S), Y > B, Y < S.
gap(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), bigcol(X), smallcol(X), bigrow(B), seprow(S), Y < B, Y > S.

why: exactly the background cells in the bars' shared columns, between the longer bar and the separator, become 4

reading: A ragged band of 2s crosses the grid; in each column everything above the column's first 2 is cleared to 0 and everything below it (except 2s) becomes the grid's other colour; columns with no 2 are cleared.

new_rows.name: above2
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 2.
top2(X, min(Y)) :- two(Y, X).
below2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), top2(X, T), Y > T, !two(Y, X).
above2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !two(Y, X), !below2(Y, X).

new_rows.name: below2
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 2.
top2(X, min(Y)) :- two(Y, X).
below2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), top2(X, T), Y > T, !two(Y, X).

why: per column: cells above the topmost 2 are 0, cells below it that are not 2 are the non-2 foreground colour (1/5/8 per pair); 2 cells unchanged

reading: Several 2-shapes (V/U shapes) have cavities; scattered loose cells of another colour (9) are removed and poured into the cavity of the one shape whose cavity size equals the number of loose cells.

slots.containers: objects of the shape colour (2) with open cavities (background cells between their cells on a row)
slots.match: container whose cavity cell count equals the piece count
slots.result: that cavity filled with the piece colour; pieces erased to background; other containers untouched

why: count of 9 cells in input = cavity size of the filled shape; output has 9 only in that cavity

reading: A 7x7 key block of 1s shows four colours at its inner corners (1,1),(1,5),(5,1),(5,5); the output is a 7x7 grid where each corner 3x3 holds the 3x3 shape of the colour shown at that key position; shapes of colours not in the key are dropped.

slots.key: the 7x7 block of 1s with four coloured cells
slots.placement: key colour at (1,1)->rows0-2 cols0-2, (1,5)->rows0-2 cols4-6, (5,1)->rows4-6 cols0-2, (5,5)->rows4-6 cols4-6

why: output is 7x7; each quadrant equals the box of the piece whose colour sits at the matching key corner

reading: A field of 8 bars (2 cells thick, separated by 0 lines) contains one 2x2 block of 6; 8 cells inside the X-shaped cone from the 6 block that opens along the bars' length (excluding the 6's own bar) turn to 4.

slots.units: across-bar distance a in bars (period 3 cells), along-bar distance k in 2-cell steps aligned to the 6 block
slots.subject: 8 cells with a >= 1 and k >= a

why: exactly the 8 cells with across-distance a>=1 and along-distance k>=a become 4; orientation follows the bars (horizontal in pair 1, vertical in pairs 2-3)

reading: A framed key line lists colours along one side; a parallel line of marks across the field is compared position by position with the key: a mark matching its key colour moves toward the key (next to the frame's separator), a mismatched mark moves to the far border.

slots.key: the colour cells inside the frame strip, one per row/column
slots.subject: the isolated marks lying on the same rows/columns as the key cells
slots.target_match: cell next to the separator line (toward the key)

why: each mark keeps its row/column; it lands adjacent to the separator iff its colour equals the key colour in that line, else on the far border
